blocks.p: Percent means per hundred. Every percent question is one of three moves: find a part, find the whole, or find the change. Write the move down before computing.

list: Successive percents multiply as decimals: 20% off then 10% off is $0.8\times 0.9=0.72$, not 30% off.
Area and volume scale by the product of the side factors: $0.7\times 1.15=0.805$, so $19.5\%$ smaller.

questions.statement: A department store marks a winter coat, originally priced at $120$, down by $25\%$ for its end-of-season sale. An additional loyalty coupon cannot be combined with sale prices. What does a customer pay for the coat at the sale price?
questions.explain: A 25% discount means paying 75%: $120\times 0.75=90$.

questions.statement: A school newspaper surveys 183 students about the new lunch menu. Of those surveyed, 47 say they prefer the new menu. To the nearest $1\%$, what percent of surveyed students prefer the new menu?
questions.explain: $\frac{47}{183}\times 100\%\approx 25.7\%$, which rounds to $26\%$.

questions.statement: A rectangular garden is redesigned so its length becomes $70\%$ of the original length and its width becomes $115\%$ of the original width. By what percent is the new area smaller than the original area?
questions.explain: Area scales by $0.70\times 1.15=0.805$, so the new area is $80.5\%$ of the old — $19.5\%$ smaller.

questions.statement: An electronics store advertises a laptop originally priced at $200$. At checkout, a $20\%$ coupon is applied first, and then a $10\%$ storewide promotion is applied to the reduced price. What is the final price?
questions.explain: Apply one at a time: $200\times 0.8=160$, then $160\times 0.9=144$. Stacked discounts never simply add.

questions.statement: After her annual review, Priya's salary increases from $52{,}000$ dollars to $58{,}900$ dollars. To the nearest tenth of a percent, what was the percent increase?

A restaurant bill totals $64$ dollars before tax. The local sales tax is $8\%$, and the diners leave an $18\%$ tip calculated on the pre-tax bill. What is the total amount paid, including tax and tip?

A salesperson earns $6\%$ commission on the first $50{,}000$ dollars of sales and $9\%$ on any amount above that. If her total sales for the month are $80{,}000$ dollars, how much commission does she earn?
A town's population of $12{,}000$ falls by $15\%$ one year and then rises by $15\%$ the next year. What is the population after the two changes?
questions.explain: $12{,}000\times 0.85\times 1.15=12{,}000\times 0.9775=11{,}730$. Equal percent moves do not cancel — the base changes.

questions.statement: A chemist has $40$ liters of a $15\%$ acid solution. She adds $10$ liters of pure water. What percent of the new mixture is acid?
questions.explain: Acid stays $0.15(40)=6$ liters while volume becomes $50$ liters: $\frac{6}{50}=12\%$.

questions.statement: After receiving a $12\%$ raise, an employee now earns $61{,}600$ dollars. What was the salary before the raise?
questions.explain: Divide by what was paid: $61{,}600\div 1.12=55{,}000$. Never subtract $12\%$ of the new salary.

blocks.p: A ratio compares quantities with the same units. A proportion sets two ratios equal. Nearly every ACT ratio word problem is one of four moves: split a total by parts, scale by a unit rate, cross-multiply a proportion, or flip it for inverse proportion. Name the move before you compute.

list: Parts split: total $\div$ total parts = one part. Ratio $2{:}3{:}5$ with total $240$ gives one part $24$.
Unit rate: reduce to one unit first. $420$ miles on $15$ gallons is $28$ mpg.
Proportion: $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}$ cross-multiplies to $ad=bc$. Map scales live here.
Three-part chains: force a common middle. $A{:}B=3{:}4$, $B{:}C=5{:}6$ becomes $15{:}20{:}24$.

blocks.p: Scale and similarity are proportions in costume. Length scale $k$ means area scales by $k^2$ and volume by $k^3$. A $3{:}5$ edge ratio gives a $9{:}25$ area ratio. Forgetting to square is the number-one hard-question trap.

list: Direct: more workers, more output. Inverse: more workers, fewer days — multiply to a constant ($6$ workers $\times$ $12$ days $= 72$ worker-days).
Mixtures: track the pure stuff, never the percent. $15\%$ of $40$ L is $6$ L of acid; water added later never changes the $6$.
Percent-ratio hybrids: convert the percent to a ratio first. $20\%$ off means price ratio $4{:}5$.

questions.statement: A summer program enrolls $32$ students, and the ratio of boys to girls is $5{:}3$. The counselors want equal-sized activity groups with no mixing across cabins. How many boys are enrolled?
questions.explain: Total parts $5+3=8$; one part is $32\div 8=4$. Boys: $5\times 4=20$. A picks the girls; D divides by the wrong part.

questions.statement: A highway map uses a scale of $1$ inch to $25$ miles. A family measures the route between two rest stops as $3.6$ inches on the map. They drive at a steady $60$ mph. How many miles long is that stretch?
questions.explain: Proportion: $3.6\times 25=90$ miles. The $60$ mph is decoration — the question asks for miles, not hours.

questions.statement: A bakery keeps its flour-to-sugar ratio at $5{:}2$ for a signature loaf. A morning batch uses $15$ cups of flour because of a bulk delivery. How many cups of sugar does that batch require?
questions.explain: One flour part is $15\div 5=3$ cups, so sugar is $2\times 3=6$ cups. C scales by $1.5$ instead of the part value.

questions.statement: A delivery van travels $420$ miles on $15$ gallons of gas. The dispatcher assigns a $196$-mile route tomorrow and wants the exact fuel needed at the same efficiency. How many gallons are required?
questions.explain: Unit rate $420\div 15=28$ mpg. Then $196\div 28=7$ gallons. Reduce to one unit first, then scale up.

questions.statement: Three volunteers split a $\$240$ prize in the ratio $2{:}3{:}5$ based on hours worked. The organizer hands each share in cash. What is the smallest share?
questions.explain: Total parts $10$; one part $240\div 10=24$. Smallest: $2\times 24=48$. D is the middle share, not the smallest.

questions.statement: Two rectangular garden plots are similar, with side lengths in the ratio $3{:}5$. The smaller plot has area $54$ square meters. A landscaper prices sod by area. What is the area of the larger plot?
questions.explain: Area ratio is $3^2{:}5^2=9{:}25$. One area part is $54\div 9=6$, so larger is $25\times 6=150$. A scales linearly and forgets to square.

questions.statement: A crew of $6$ painters finishes a warehouse in $12$ days working at the same pace. The deadline moves up, so the foreman raises the crew to $9$ painters at the same pace. How many days will the job take now?
questions.explain: Worker-days constant: $6\times 12=72$. Then $72\div 9=8$ days. More workers means fewer days — direct division $12\div 9$ is the trap.

questions.statement: A lab mixes acid and water in the ratio $3{:}2$ to make $45$ liters of cleaning solution. An inspector tests the acid content only. How many liters of acid are in the batch?
questions.explain: Total parts $5$; one part $45\div 5=9$. Acid: $3\times 9=27$ L. A is the water share.

questions.statement: A $\$144{,}000$ grant is divided among three labs in the ratio $2{:}3{:}7$. The middle lab spends its share on equipment. How much does the middle lab receive?
questions.explain: Total parts $12$; one part $144{,}000\div 12=12{,}000$. Middle: $3\times 12{,}000=36{,}000$. D is the largest share.

questions.statement: An architect's floor plan uses $1$ cm to $4$ m. A conference room measures $3.25$ cm by $4.5$ cm on the plan. The client wants the real floor area for carpet. What is it, in square meters?
questions.explain: Real sides: $3.25\times 4=13$ m and $4.5\times 4=18$ m. Area $13\times 18=234$. A multiplies plan area by $4$ once instead of scaling each side.

questions.statement: Two laptops sell in the price ratio $4{:}7$. The expensive model costs $\$21$ more than the basic model during a sale. What is the price of the basic model?
questions.explain: Gap parts $7-4=3$ equal $\$21$, so one part is $\$7$. Basic: $4\times 7=28$. D is the expensive model.

questions.statement: Two freight trains leave a yard at the same time on parallel tracks, with speeds in the ratio $5{:}8$. After the same travel time, the faster train is $45$ miles ahead. A dispatcher needs the slower train's distance. How far has it traveled?
questions.explain: Gap parts $3$ equal $45$ miles, so one part is $15$. Slower: $5\times 15=75$ miles. Equal times mean distances share the speed ratio.

questions.statement: A foundry casts an alloy with copper and zinc in the ratio $7{:}5$. A crucible holds $42$ kg of copper for a pour. How many kilograms of zinc must be added to keep the ratio?
questions.explain: One copper part is $42\div 7=6$ kg, so zinc is $5\times 6=30$ kg. Cross-multiplying $7/5=42/z$ gives the same $z=30$.

questions.statement: A contractor mixes red, blue, and white paint in the ratio $4{:}3{:}1$ for $24$ gallons of custom color. The supplier runs short on blue pigment. How many gallons of blue paint does the full order need?
questions.explain: Total parts $8$; one part $24\div 8=3$ gallons. Blue: $3\times 3=9$ gallons. D doubles the blue parts.

questions.statement: A robotics club starts with boys and girls in the ratio $3{:}5$. Then $8$ new girls join and no boys join, making the ratio $1{:}2$. The advisor needs the original boy count for uniforms. How many boys were there at the start?
questions.explain: Let parts be $k$: $3k/(5k+8)=1/2$, so $6k=5k+8$ and $k=8$. Boys: $3\times 8=24$. Check: $24$ to $48$ is $1{:}2$.

questions.statement: Two delivery trucks travel for the same time with speeds in the ratio $7{:}9$. The faster truck covers $36$ miles more than the slower one. How many miles does the slower truck cover?
questions.explain: Gap parts $2$ equal $36$ miles, so one part is $18$. Slower: $7\times 18=126$ miles. Same time means distance ratio equals speed ratio.

questions.statement: A pastry chef holds flour, sugar, and butter in the ratio $6{:}4{:}3$. A holiday order uses $2.5$ cups of sugar. How many cups of flour does it need?
questions.explain: One sugar part is $2.5\div 4=0.625$ cups. Flour: $6\times 0.625=3.75$ cups. B rounds the part value early.

questions.statement: A trail map has scale $1{:}50{,}000$. A scout measures $8.4$ cm between two camps on the map. The troop hikes in kilometers. What is the real distance?
questions.explain: Real cm: $8.4\times 50{,}000=420{,}000$ cm $=4{,}200$ m $=4.2$ km. C misses the cm-to-km conversion ($100{,}000$ cm per km).

questions.statement: Two bottling machines run together with output rates in the ratio $3{:}2$, producing $30$ bottles per minute combined. An engineer isolates the faster machine for testing. How many bottles per minute does it produce alone?
questions.explain: Total parts $5$; one part $30\div 5=6$. Faster: $3\times 6=18$ per minute. A is the slower machine.

questions.statement: Four identical pumps drain a flooded basement in $9$ hours. The crew brings in two more identical pumps, for $6$ total, all at the same rate. How long will draining take now?
questions.explain: Pump-hours constant: $4\times 9=36$. Then $36\div 6=6$ hours. D divides the wrong direction.

questions.statement: Three assembly lines produce at rates in the ratio $2{:}3{:}4$, with $1{,}080$ units total in a shift. Quality control audits the fastest line's full output. How many units is that?
questions.explain: Total parts $9$; one part $1{,}080\div 9=120$. Fastest: $4\times 120=480$ units. A is the slowest line.

questions.statement: Two similar storage cubes have edge lengths in the ratio $2{:}3$. The smaller cube holds $64$ cubic feet. The buyer wants the larger cube's capacity. What is it?
questions.explain: Volume ratio is $2^3{:}3^3=8{:}27$. One part is $64\div 8=8$, so larger is $27\times 8=216$. B scales by area ($4{:}9$) instead of volume.

questions.statement: A chemist has $15$ liters of $20\%$ salt solution and adds some $50\%$ solution to reach a $30\%$ mixture. She tracks pure salt only. How many liters of $50\%$ solution must she add?
A shelter starts with dogs and cats in the ratio $5{:}3$. After $12$ dogs are adopted and no cats leave, the ratio becomes $1{:}1$. How many cats are there?
questions.explain: Let $k$ be the part: $5k-12=3k$, so $2k=12$ and $k=6$. Cats: $3\times 6=18$. Verify: $30-12=18$ dogs equals $18$ cats.

questions.statement: Two cyclists start together on a $60$-mile charity ride at steady speeds of $16$ mph and $20$ mph. The organizer at the finish wants the gap between them when the faster rider finishes. How many miles behind is the slower rider then?
questions.explain: Faster takes $60\div 20=3$ hr. Slower covers $16\times 3=48$ miles, so the gap is $60-48=12$ miles. C uses a $2.5$-hr guess instead of the true $3$-hr time.

questions.statement: Two meshed gears have teeth in the ratio $8{:}5$ (large to small). The large gear turns $120$ times during a test run. Because rotations run inverse to teeth, how many times does the small gear turn?
questions.explain: Rotations ratio is $5{:}8$. Small turns $120\times 8\div 5=192$ times. A multiplies by $5/8$ instead of flipping.

questions.statement: A bank exchanges dollars to euros at $\$1=0.90$ euros, then charges a $2\%$ fee on the euro amount. A traveler exchanges $\$500$ for a homestay deposit. How many euros does she receive?
questions.explain: Gross euros: $500\times 0.90=450$. After the fee keep $98\%$: $450\times 0.98=441$. C forgets the fee.

questions.statement: A $6$-foot pole casts a $9$-foot shadow. At the same time, a courthouse casts a $51$-foot shadow. A surveyor needs the courthouse height. What is it, in feet?
questions.explain: Same sun angle: $6/9=h/51$, so $h=51\times 6\div 9=34$ ft. B flips a ratio.

questions.statement: Three funds hold money with $A{:}B=3{:}4$ and $B{:}C=5{:}6$. An auditor finds $\$45{,}000$ in fund A. How much is in fund C?
A $2.5$-kg brine has salt and water in the ratio $1{:}9$ by mass. A cook adds $0.5$ kg of pure water for soup stock. What percent of the new mixture is salt?
questions.explain: Salt stays $2.5\div 10=0.25$ kg; new total $3.0$ kg. Percent: $0.25\div 3.0\approx 8.33\%$. A divides by $3.125$ instead of $3.0$.
